site.name: Kanonengasse
site.boundary: Suitable by traffic, middle vertex in a Fokus heat area, named; most active or upcoming permits within 60 m (ties: longer). The street and its numbers are computed from open data; the drawing is a generic schematic, not this street's geometry.

layers.label: Known now
layers.question: What can we responsibly say before a site visit?
layers.summary: Open records and their reproducible readings at this street. They do not describe what lies under it.

layers.label: Derived carefully
layers.question: What hypotheses can computation make visible?
layers.summary: Corridor surfaces and ranges from declared assumptions. Unvalidated; for explaining and screening.

layers.label: Must ask or measure
layers.question: What stops this becoming a recommendation?
layers.summary: Seven facts are gated or need a site check. Each names who holds it and the next action.

claims.title: Is the street in a heat focus area?
claims.method: Read from the published layer at the street.
claims.limitation: A published layer read at the street; it says nothing about what lies under it.

claims.title: Does the canton rate it sponge-suitable by traffic?
claims.method: Read from the published layer at the street. Reading: geeignet (< 2000 vehicles/day).
claims.limitation: A published layer read at the street; it says nothing about what lies under it.

claims.title: How many cadastre trees stand in the corridor?
claims.method: Read from the published layer at the street.
claims.limitation: A published layer read at the street; it says nothing about what lies under it.

claims.title: Is the street in a groundwater protection zone?
claims.method: Read from the published layer at the street.
claims.limitation: Tested at the middle vertex only

claims.title: How deep is groundwater nearby?
claims.unit: derived minimum depth at Steinenparking (1060), 164 m away
claims.method: Terrain height minus 10-year maximum level Reading: 13.1 m below ground at its shallowest (Steinenparking (1060), 164 m away).
claims.limitation: A station is a point, not a depth map. Infiltration needs a site test

claims.title: Will the street be opened soon anyway?
claims.unit: active or upcoming permits within 60 m
claims.method: Permit points within the radius of the line; category by keyword Reading: 24 active or upcoming permits within 60 m (24 utility), ending 202612, 202704.
claims.limitation: Permits are not a coordinated works plan. Snapshot 2026-10-03T20:36:22.296Z

claims.title: How much sealed ground is in the corridor?
claims.method: 1 m grid samples within the half width of the line, classed by the land-cover polygon they fall in; road plus other paving
claims.limitation: Corridor of 12 m either side of the line: includes both pavements and building edges. Land-cover classes say what the surface is, not how it is built or where it drains

claims.title: How much planted ground is in the corridor?
claims.method: 1 m grid samples within the half width of the line, classed by the land-cover polygon they fall in
claims.limitation: Corridor of 12 m either side of the line: includes both pavements and building edges. Land-cover classes say what the surface is, not how it is built or where it drains

claims.title: Do those trees stand in mapped planted ground?
claims.unit: trees without a mapped planted polygon
claims.method: Tree point in a planted land-cover polygon Reading: 2 of 2 have no mapped planted polygon at the point.
claims.limitation: Does not mean sealed paving. Does not reveal pit size

claims.title: 30 mm rain on the corridor's sealed ground
claims.limitation: Where the water goes. Flood-risk reduction

claims.title: One 20 m² sponge element could hold
claims.method: A × d × n for one element; depth 0.25–0.45 m, voids 0.2–0.35 assumed
claims.limitation: Infiltration. Hydraulic performance. Whether the element can be built

claims.title: Which drainage system serves this area?
claims.source: Tiefbauamt and Amt für Umwelt und Energie
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.gatekeeper: Tiefbauamt and Amt für Umwelt und Energie
claims.unlock_action: Digitise the published 2012 GEP drainage-system map (1:20,000) at this street
claims.decision_blocked: Whether to infiltrate, retain or connect an overflow

claims.title: Is there a line under the footprint?
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.unlock_action: Order a Leitungskataster extract for the footprint plus 5 m, stated as early planning
claims.decision_blocked: Whether digging here can go to detailed design

claims.title: How deep are the lines?
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.unlock_action: Ask the operators named on the extract for depths in the footprint
claims.decision_blocked: How deep a trench or pit may go

claims.title: Does water soak away here?
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.unlock_action: Commission an infiltration test at the footprint
claims.decision_blocked: Whether infiltration is a credible mechanism

claims.title: Where may overflow water go?
claims.source: Tiefbauamt and Amt für Umwelt und Energie
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.gatekeeper: Tiefbauamt and Amt für Umwelt und Energie
claims.unlock_action: Ask Tiefbauamt where overflow from the footprint may discharge
claims.decision_blocked: Whether the design may rely on an overflow connection

claims.title: What lies under the asphalt?
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.unlock_action: Core the pavement while the street is open for the permitted works
claims.decision_blocked: Excavation cost and the depth of new soil

claims.title: Where are the gullies and kerb inlets?
claims.source: Leitungskataster (Grundbuch- und Vermessungsamt) + Residents and team
claims.limitation: Not in the open data reviewed.
claims.gatekeeper: Leitungskataster (Grundbuch- und Vermessungsamt) + Residents and team
claims.unlock_action: Mark visible inlets on the orthophoto; check the Leitungskataster extract
claims.decision_blocked: Where road water can be led into green

intervention.name: Tree trench or rain garden in the corridor
intervention.why: The street is opened anyway (24 utility permits nearby). A sponge element could ride on those works.

scenario.note: Rainfall depth × assumed element footprint only. It is not retained volume, flood reduction or design performance.
